I'll start by saying that 1.) I'm a new player that bought the game recently, and 2.) despite not recommending this game, I do enjoy the gameplay. The singular issue that prevents me from recommending this game, is that there is STILL a game-breaking bug that, as far as I can tell after a quick google search, has persisted since September of 2017. This bug causes you to be completely incapable of getting new equipment, stating that your save file is corrupted each and every time you get an item at the end of a run. In other words, it's completely impossible for new players to progress in terms of equipment, and many older players are coming back to the game after a break to discover their save file is corrupted.  

There are supposedly a couple of things that can be done in an attempt to circumvent this bug, including deleting a particular file and allowing steam to redownload it, and installing the vanguard version of the game and running that first, though I've read from several posts that for some people neither of these solutions work. Frankly, in either case, neither of these steps should be necessary, and the fact that they still are after [b]FIVE YEARS[/b] is just unacceptable. Had I been aware of this problem before hand, I would not have bought the game at all. If you don't care about the equipment and are simply looking for a fun archery game, I suppose Quivr can still accomplish that, but I'll leave you to exercise your own judgement.

Will It VR?: Right on target. (But with an important, easy bug fix. Read Below!)

VR seems like it was made for archery games. Unlike holding a gun in VR, pulling a bow feels natural and intuitive. QuiVr delivers that gameplay in a simple but engaging loop that has kept me coming back.

QUICK BUG FIX TIP: Right now, QuiVr seems to have a bug that keeps you from collecting equipment. You can fix this issue by running QuiVr Vanguard once. If you do that, QuiVr should work correctly.

QuiVr has come a long way from its simple static, wave-after-wave gameplay (though that experience is still available via QuiVr Vanguard). It's still a wave shooter, but there's a lot more to it. Power-ups, boss critters, enemies that require tactical thinking, and puzzle levels all round out the experience. Do it right and you'll get a piece of equipment that you can use, and you can upgrade and enchant your equipment as well. There are a lot of simple subsystems mixed in - not so much that they're distracting, but enough to give the experience a more polished and immersive feel.

QuiVr shines in multiplayer, where you can team up to cover all your angles and have each others' backs. Puzzle levels scale up to player number as well, so the challenge stays solid.

[h1]迫りくる化け物を地道に一匹ずつ射抜いていくVR弓矢ゲー。[/h1]
もうちょっとで素直にサムズアップにできたのに惜しい、くらいの評価。

[list]
	[*]移動は特定地点へのテレポートのみ
	[*]スナップ回転は 45度 のみ
	[*]下方向で180度ターンはなし
[/list]

[h1]■概要■[/h1]
タワーディフェンスのように巨大な門に向かって化け物が押し寄せてくるが、タレットを設置する能力はないので自らが半固定砲台となって弓矢でひたすら駆逐し続ける弓矢ゲー。

谷底を進む敵に対して城門や左右の崖の上に何箇所か狙撃場所が用意されており、そこにあるポータルを射抜くことでその地点へテレポートして応戦する。敵の処理が追いつかなくなってきたら退がる程度で、滅多に移動はせずVR酔いとも縁遠い。

守るべき門のライフゲージがなくなると敗北だが、その前に敵の死体から集まる霊魂ゲージみたいな物が貯まると敵が湧いてくる上流方向のエリアへ移動して、そこに新たな門を建てる形で定期的に戦闘エリアが変化していく。

数エリアごとに巨大ボスとの戦闘があり勝利すると誤差レベルで性能が違う装備などが貰えるが、特にクリアとかの概念はないのかすぐにまた次のエリアへと続いていく、常にエンドレスモードの様なゲームシステム。

オンラインCOOPも可能だが、特にストーリーの進行度とかがあるわけでなし、途中参加 / 退出も自由なゆる～いCOOPになっている。

[h1]■弓矢と戦闘■[/h1]
Quiver（矢筒・えびら）とVRを掛け合わせたタイトル通り矢は背中（or お尻）の矢筒から取り出して番える必要があり、また弦を限界近くまで引き絞った状態でちょっと待つとAimed Shotと呼ばれる高威力の矢を放てる。

ものは弓矢なのに矢継ぎ早に数を撃つよりも、一射一射に魂を込めて射るほうが掃滅力は高い。とはいえ溜めて射ったのに外すとタイムロスがでかいので、慣れないうちは当て勘を養うために数をこなすのも大事。

時々敵が特殊効果付きの矢を撃てるアイテムを落とす他、手袋には時間経過で回復する魔法が篭められており投擲することも可能。初期装備だと手榴弾のような性能だが、クールダウンが長いわりに範囲が狭いのでいざという時に頼りにならない。

[h1]■感想■[/h1]
背中から矢を引き抜き、番えて引き絞り、放つ。この一連の動作がシンプルに楽しい。クールダウンが終わり次第スキルを発動させないとDPSが落ちるとかそういう余計なことは一切考えなくていいし、一心不乱に続けていると段々クセになる。

基本的に高所からの撃ち下ろしなので上下方向の狙いのズレも分かりやすいし、主観視点だけど状況の把握も比較的容易で、わりと頭空っぽにしてても遊べる。また定期的に戦闘エリアが様変わりしていくのも飽きなくていい。

ボスドロップで火力が1.2％UPする弓みたいなLoot box要素に関しては心底どうでもいいが、ゲームそのものは基本的に好感触。冒頭で書いたとおり、「文句なしにオススメする」にあと一歩で届きそうくらいの感じではある。

ただ、何種類かいる内で、サイコロを積み上げたトーテムポールのようなボスが不快すぎる。

ボスの周囲を動き回る球体を全て射抜けばクリアというミニゲームのようなボス戦なのだが、妨害として強制的に視界を暗転させてくる。HMDを被って視覚全てをそれに依存した状態で目隠しされるだけでうざいのに、その目隠しをパカパカと1～2秒周期で開けたり閉めたり開けたり閉めたりされるとただただストレスしか感じない。

I want QuiVR to be good, I waited a few years for it to come out of early access, and sadly it might be the best archery simulator, but I still cannot recommend it because there's so many issues that hold it back.

To start I want to shout out top players rett and Brookcowboy for playing with me and being nice showing a newer player the ropes. These guys have 400+ hours in QuiVR and I'm really glad this game has enough end-game content that it can deliver to those dedicated players.

My biggest tripping point that I have to get off my chest before anything else is not being able to turn incrementally and having to spin 360 in my room and then hit my chair and walls when I have to draw the bow in an unexpected direction. There is no excuse for not having a 45/90 degree incremental turn functionality.

QuiVR has solid archery mechanics, provided that you can get the offset right to start since there are three sliders (horizontal, vertical, and angle) that could be messed up and make it feel like garbage, but once those feel right the bow mechanics are good and you better enjoy them or else this game is gonna get old real fast because you're gonna be shooting thousands of arrows and doing nothing else. There is no prediction or guide to help so all your shots are free aim, so you've really gotta get that muscle memory and hand eye coordination to even get past the first few enemies.

At its core QuiVR is a wave shooter but the waves are coming at a stationary gate and you can move between set spots in the valley, but the reason this is frustrating is that these spots always have a blind spot so if there is an enemy right below you about to reach your gate and you can't get a line on it or missed your window of opportunity you have to teleport to a further spot (by shooting an arrow at it which you can also spend quite a few shots failing at) to even continue aiming at it. It is because of this that the skill curve is very steep requiring the skill to shoot the small moving targets with no guide before you can even get to the first boss.

The bosses are the most exciting part of this game, but sadly they are a prime example of something that is a pain point throughout this game: no hints at what you're supposed to be doing. There are so many times even in menus or the gear upgrade system where I don't even know what button I'm supposed to push to activate the upgrade or where I get an item reward and it says right in front of me "would you like to equip? - Yes - No" and I can't even get the popup to disappear clicking every button over Yes but nothing in response. Back to the bosses, I've seen so many requests for help on the bosses like "what the hell am I even supposed to do here?" my experience with a Tremors style earth worm would have been fantastic if it was clear that the obscured red circles near the ground are the things to shoot at instead of the big spears sticking out of his face that are similar to the weak points of another boss.
Similar to this I finally found a post about the new "elite" system from 10/19/18 that says hey watch out elites can now have modifiers, but there is no explanation of that in the game. I am a huge fan of exploration in games but I'm shooting at these enemies and the arrows are bouncing off, being sent flying in random directions and occasionally those thrown off arrows are hitting portals super far away that I can't even get back to the fight because I can't hit the portals to take me back and my run is over because of it. There needs to be a minimal amount of info at least when presented with new obstacles.

My final qualm is the gear system. It definitely works if you are a dedicated player coming back for days and weeks to this game, but it does not feel respectful of the player's time to me. Each run you can get random gear and points and can spend those points in a lotto style gear upgrade system, but getting good gear and rolling good upgrades takes hours worth of grinding, so if you enjoy the game this will add replayability but unless you have done this don't expect to make it very far in the game once certain enemies show up that you have no option of even damaging because they will spit your arrows right back at you and its game over.

I get terrible performance on this game. This is a threadripper 3970x and 2080 TI and I get around 35 FPS looking into the distance even at half resolution. Looking at the ground I get 300 FPS. Other games are absolutely fine in comparison.

To be clear, it's a very fun game (at least as much as I played it), but it's unsuitable for "Standing" (small space) setup, unless you have the space to turn around 360° with your eyes closed and arms stretched out, without hitting anything.

It's very fun while I can play without turning around, but the moment I find a spot where I have to turn around 180°, to shift between targets that are comming at me and targets that already passed me and are now behind me, I played the game about 3 times and I ended up hitting furniture each time. There's no real damage done yet, but I can easily see myself breaking off the outer "guard" of the index knuckle with the force I used last 3 times.

Other games solve that problem by 45° snap turning on right thumbstick, but this one doesn't have it. Odd, because I've seen requests for this feature dating back to 2016. Developer even responded, but it never made it to the game.

Another minor flaw: Lack of information about what anything does. You get a tutorial early on (which is great), because it covers gameplay, but I couldn't figure out what some of the menu options do, despite having a rough idea of what they SHOULD do. I could have sworn I've seen an option that would fix my previous problem, but it didn't do anything.... Oculus exclusive feature?

Anyways, if you've got enough space to play in it's a fun game.

I bought the game Elven Assassin because I liked the idea of a VR Tower Defense game where the players are the towers. I also liked the fantasy setting of Orcs and Dragons and whatnot. While I enjoyed the game it lacked progress and customization.  While looking at reviews for the game I saw a couple posts saying that QuiVR was a similar game but better so I decided to check it out. I checked out a gameplay video by a YouTuber followed by a quick 15 minute dive into the Demo (which seems to be from a much older build of the game and doesn't quite do it justice)

While not quite a huge fan of the games setting and enemy design I can appreciate it. It is creative and gives the enemies unique abilities that makes you think a little before releasing your arrow. The game feels much smoother with better arrow mechanics and better options for progression and progress. I highly recommend this game if you are looking for a bow and arrow based tower defense style game.

Pros:
Best bow and arrow physics I've found so far
Progression via lootable gear options that grant unique options for arrow and magic abilities
Unique bossfight/minigames that are fun, interesting, challenging, and rewarding
Drop in multiplayer co-op

Cons:
Slightly repetitive gameplay. While the maps do change its still in the same setting with the same familiar enemies and repetitive boss fights.
There aren't too many spells available to choose from via gear. Elven Assassin offers two spell trees to choose from with unlockable spells or cooldown reduction you can pick with spell points you earn by leveling up. 


And thats about it for now. I will update as I play more but so far the game is very fun and promising!

I also can recommend to play it in Multiplayer.

Even if it's strangers.
And I also learn from more expierienced players how they position, what spells the use when and
generally how those bosses and bonus games work.

Really nice.
The only thing I'd like to see would be more catchy hit sounds.

100% recommended for people that like bow mechanics in VR.

Thoroughly enjoyable game. I was looking for a good VR archery game after enjoying the one in Valve's 'The Lab'. I've only just got my Rift and was amazed at how good archery could feel in VR. A few suggestions for QuiVR came up while I was searching and I tried the demo, loved it, and immediately bought the full game after. The bow feels very solid and satisfying, and shooting never gets old. Click turning, as an option, has been much appreciated because I don't have a lot of room in my flat (I stand in one place and can't do roomscale). As a bonus, my weedy arms get a bit of a workout playing this! I like the visuals and the sense of humour too. This game was just what I was looking for.

Brilliant archery game.

My only complaint: Lots of new players go straight into multiplayer and goof around, making it difficult or impossible to win. However, I found the community great and while it is fun solo, it gets so much better multiplayer.

QuiVR will hold a special place in my heart as one of the first VR games I sank a lot of time into. The developer was constantly was adding new content and trying new things to explore what is possible in VR so there was always something new and interesting to try out.

It's changed a lot since the free demo. There is a lot more content now but I think they lost something along the way. Even though it's not quite as great as I hoped it would become it's still a pretty fun experience and the developer has proven he's worth supporting.
